topic: identifying SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL evidence

problems.desc: Name the congruence criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS or HL) justified by each of six given-lists, and identify the one arrangement that is not a criterion — short written answers
Name the criterion the marks justify and state what the shared diagonal contributes (reflexive property) — written justification
Name the criterion the marks justify and state which pair of angles is supplied by the vertical-angle theorem — written justification
Decide whether the marked evidence is ASA or AAS for the side named, and explain why the two criteria are interchangeable once the third angle is known — written justification
Explain why HL is a valid criterion for right triangles by naming what the Pythagorean theorem determines — written justification
Explain why side-side-angle is not a congruence criterion and describe the two-triangle counterexample shown — open written reasoning
Two-column proof that the diagonal of a parallelogram splits it into two congruent triangles, ending in a named criterion — open proof
Judge a claim that side-side-angle evidence proves congruence, name the arrangement correctly, and state what extra given would rescue the argument — open written reasoning
